doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jazz rock, volume and booking Sun Ra
summary: He dislikes loud small bands but booked Sun Ra for Gilmore and Patrick.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: So do you - just to talk about your taste within the music itself, and just thinking about those particular periods of time where the jazz itself started to go in various directions there. We’re talking about the jazz rock era, and I know there’s some of the musicians that came through that particular period of time that I’ve seen on here through some of the posters. How did that fair within your interest in the music? Was it something that you embraced, or do you find that that integration of the electronic music and jazz rock was something that maybe didn’t have? Because remember, we’re talking volume, I wasn’t sure if I heard you before, volume becomes an issue too. Is that something that you weren’t so crazy about?

Yeah. When a five-piece band is louder than an eighteen-piece big band, something’s wrong as far as I’m concerned. But I even got into the weird stuff with Sun Ra, you know, and he was a trip. He’s funny; he started to believe his own bullshit.
[Laughs] Did he do well when you booked him?
Yeah, yeah. I booked him mostly because of John Gilmore and Pat Patrick on the band.
